translations.literal: he decreed that Jiji execute Lingde at Suizhou and Wang Sitong execute Lingxi at Xuzhou,
translations.idiomatic: he ordered Jiji to execute Lingde at Suizhou and Wang Sitong to execute Lingxi at Xuzhou,

sentences.zh: （吳縝《篡誤》云：《史彥瓊傳》，友謙有子建徽被殺。

translations.literal: (Wu Zhen's Errors of Usurpation says: In the Biography of Shi Yanqiong, Youqian had a son Jianhui who was killed.
translations.idiomatic: (According to Wu Zhen's Errors of Usurpation, the Biography of Shi Yanqiong records that Youqian's son Jianhui was killed,

sentences.zh: 傳中未載。）〉

translations.literal: but this is not recorded in the biography.)]
translations.idiomatic: though this is not recorded in the main biography.)]

sentences.zh: 命夏魯奇誅其族於河中。

translations.literal: He ordered Xia Luqi to exterminate his clan at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xia Luqi to exterminate his clan at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 初，魯奇至，友謙妻張氏率其家屬二百餘口見魯奇曰：「請疏骨肉名字，無致他人橫死。

translations.literal: When Luqi first arrived, Youqian's wife Lady Zhang led more than two hundred members of the family to see Luqi and said: "I beg you to list the names of our kin by blood, that others may not die unjustly."
translations.idiomatic: When Luqi arrived, Lady Zhang led more than two hundred family members to meet him and said, "Please list our kin by name so that no innocent may die by mistake."

sentences.zh: 」將刑，張氏持先賜鐵券授魯奇曰：「皇帝所賜也。

translations.literal: " As execution was about to take place, Lady Zhang held out the iron certificate previously bestowed and gave it to Luqi, saying: "This was granted by the emperor."
translations.idiomatic: As the execution was about to begin, Lady Zhang produced the iron certificate the emperor had granted and said, "This was bestowed by the emperor himself."

sentences.zh: 」是時，百口塗地，冤酷之聲，行路流涕。

translations.literal: " At that time a hundred mouths were smeared on the ground; the sound of cruel injustice made passersby on the road weep.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred lives were destroyed; the cries of injustice moved every passerby to tears.

sentences.zh: 先是，河中衙城閽者夜見婦人數十，袨服靚妝，仆馬炫耀，自外馳騁，笑語趨衙城。

translations.literal: Earlier, the gatekeeper of the Hezhong yamen city at night saw several tens of women in splendid dress and fine makeup, with servants and horses dazzling, galloping in from outside, laughing and talking as they hurried toward the yamen city.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the yamen gatekeeper had seen dozens of women at night in splendid dress and fine makeup, with dazzling retinues of servants and horses, galloping in from outside, laughing as they rushed toward the compound.

sentences.zh: 閽者不知其故，不敢詰，至門排騎而入，既而扃鎖如故，復無人跡，乃知妖鬼也。

translations.literal: The gatekeeper did not know the reason and did not dare question; they reached the gate, pushed aside the riders and entered; afterward the bolts were locked as before and again there were no human traces—then he knew they were demon spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeeper dared not question them; they pushed through the gate and entered, then the locks were fastened as before and no trace of anyone remained—he knew they were spirits.

sentences.zh: 又繼麟登逍遙樓，聞哭聲四合，詰日訊之，巷無喪者，隔歲乃族誅。

translations.literal: Moreover Jilin ascended the Xiaoyao Tower and heard wailing on all four sides; he questioned people the next day—no house in the lanes was in mourning; a year later the clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Jilin also climbed the Xiaoyao Tower and heard wailing on every side; he inquired the next day but found no mourning in the lanes; a year later his whole clan was slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 及明宗即位，始下詔昭雪焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong ascended the throne, he first issued an edict to clear their names.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Emperor Mingzong took the throne was an edict issued to clear their names.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：全義一逢亂世，十領名藩，而能免梁祖之雄猜，受莊宗之厚遇，雖由恭順，亦係貨財。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Quanyi once met a chaotic age and ten times held famous commands, yet could escape the Founder's heroic suspicion and receive Emperor Zhuangzong's generous treatment—though through deference, it also depended on wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Quanyi lived through chaotic times and held ten famous commands, yet escaped the Liang Founder's fierce suspicion and won Emperor Zhuangzong's generous favor—deference helped, but so did his wealth.

sentences.zh: 《傳》所謂「貨以藩身」者，全義得之矣。

translations.literal: What the Commentary calls "using wealth to preserve oneself in a command," Quanyi attained it.
translations.idiomatic: What the Commentary calls "using wealth to preserve oneself in office," Quanyi exemplified.

sentences.zh: 友謙向背為謀，二三其德，考其行事，亦匪純臣。

translations.literal: Youqian turned his back or faced forward as strategy required; he was inconstant in virtue; examining his conduct, he too was no pure minister.
translations.idiomatic: Youqian shifted allegiance as strategy demanded and was inconstant in loyalty; judged by his conduct, he too was no loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 然全族之誅，禍斯酷矣，得非鬼神害盈，而天道惡滿乎！

translations.literal: Yet the extermination of the whole clan—how cruel was that calamity! Was it not that spirits harm fullness and the Way of Heaven hates excess!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the slaughter of his entire clan was calamity of the cruelest kind—was it not that spirits punish excess and Heaven abhors fullness!
